text:
Jonathan Lekkerimäki finally has an NHL role, and the shot that made him a first-round pick is doing the talking. The Canucks winger has 7 goals and 18 points in 24 games, 11 of those points on the power play, after only 37 NHL games before this season. Daily Hive's Daniel Wagner talked to teammates about the release, and Brock Boeser told him: "For how little he is, he has a super-hard shot, and it's impressive."

The quality is on the power play more than at even strength. At five on five, Vancouver gets only 38.4% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, and his 7 goals came on 5.0 expected. Our talent range says his scoring rate is likely to come down from 2.93 points per 60, though not off a cliff.

For context, forwards drafted 10th to 20th since 2005 scored a median 0.35 points a game in their first full season. He's at 0.75. His ice time is climbing too, up about a minute and a half over his last ten games. Watch his even-strength shifts; that's where he still has to prove it.
